what_its_for: Bicalutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It works by blocking the effects of male hormones (like testosterone) that can help prostate cancer cells grow. It is usually used together with another hormone treatment called an LHRH analog (such as leuprolide or goserelin).
how_to_take: Take bicalutamide by mouth with or without food, once a day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is one 50 mg tablet taken once daily. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you are doing.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store bicalutamide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking warfarin (a blood thinner) without telling your doctor, as bicalutamide can increase its effects and raise your risk of bleeding. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit, as it may affect how your body processes this medicine. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should never handle crushed or broken bicalutamide tablets, as it can harm an unborn baby. Do not start any new medications — including vitamins, supplements, or herbal products — without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (signs of liver problems), dark urine or pale stools, severe nausea or stomach pain, chest pain or difficulty breathing, swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, pain or tenderness in your breasts or unusual breast growth, shortness of breath, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also tell your doctor if you feel depressed or notice any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Bicalutamide starts working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you and your doctor can see the full benefit through lab tests or scans. Do not stop taking it just because you do not notice a change quickly. It is important to keep taking it as directed, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): No dose adjustment is generally needed, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, so regular monitoring is important. Patients with liver problems: Use with caution. Your doctor will monitor your liver function with blood tests. Tell your doctor if you have any history of liver disease. Women: Bicalutamide is not approved for use in women. Pregnant women and women of childbearing age should never handle broken or crushed tablets due to the risk of harm to an unborn baby. Children: This medicine is not for use in children or teenagers. Patients with kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed, but let your doctor know about any kidney issues.
